brief: Goldman argues the recent long-end rate selloff is due for a reversal: diminished technical risk (MBS convexity near zero, reduced asset-manager duration longs, limited evidence of active foreign UST selling) plus elevated macro uncertainty, not impaired market function, drove the rise, so GS recommends receiving 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly (entry 2bp, target -4bp, stop 6bp) and selling payers given elevated implied volatility. A Thursday rally despite higher energy prices showed yields are sensitive to AI-trade confidence shocks, reinforcing the asymmetry-to-lower-yields view, though an upcoming CPI release is expected to show boosts from energy and commodity costs and seasonal distortions. In Europe, GS forecasts 10y Bunds at 3.25% by end-2026 as sovereign stress builds a safe-haven bid, expects OAT spreads to stabilise tighter since widening outstripped fundamentals, but sees BTPs still carrying too little political risk premium given Italy's 1.2ppt cumulative deficit-target revision for 2027-2028, favoring Bonos instead. For Gilts, hawkish BoE comments and the 28 October budget limit front-end rally room, though declining net supply and BoE QT should support Gilts versus swaps.
